solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Laid up face down

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word Laid is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Something was laid face down, perhaps a playing card or a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAID into DIAL; 'down' is only part of the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a clock or watch is its dial, the marked plate behind the hands.

clue.text: Notice what has to be kicked in competition

parts.note: to notice something is to spot it
a football is what gets kicked, so this phrase stands for the ball

explanation.surface: A remark that you should notice what has to be kicked in a football contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Spot the Ball is a long-running British newspaper competition where entrants mark where the ball was in a photo with it removed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a newspaper prize game, so it is one specific competition.

clue.text: Protection to put first

definitions.meaning: freedom from danger, being kept from harm
the slogan '... first' says this thing should be given top priority

explanation.definitionFit: Safety means being kept secure from harm, and the slogan says it should be put first.

clue.text: One out on his feet

parts.note: 'out on his feet' normally describes a boxer barely conscious yet standing; here it is someone asleep yet walking about

explanation.definitionFit: A somnambulist walks around while unconscious, literally asleep yet upright and moving.

clue.text: A few snowflakes — blast!

definitions.meaning: a light brief fall of snow
a sudden gust or rush of wind

explanation.definitionFit: A flurry is both a short light snowfall and a sudden gust of wind.

clue.text: Narrate story given by blabbermouth

parts.note: to narrate is to tell
a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A blabbermouth retells a story they were told.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale is someone who gossips or reports others' secrets, just like a blabbermouth.

clue.text: Firm pay without a duplicate

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: without means the letter a is taken away from the word pay

explanation.surface: A company pays out without making a second copy of its documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the A from the clue word pay; 'duplicate' reads as a verb in the surface but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy is a reproduction, a synonym of duplicate as a noun.

clue.text: Swear there's nothing missing from sequence of treatment

indicators.note: missing from means one letter is dropped out of the longer word

parts.note: a course of treatment is a sequence of doses or sessions
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone swears when a dose is missed from their course of treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing from' takes O out of COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to use bad language, a synonym of swear.

clue.text: Underworld character in outer space

definitions.meaning: the Roman god who ruled the realm of the dead
the distant dwarf planet beyond Neptune

explanation.definitionFit: Pluto is the Roman ruler of the dead and also a dwarf planet far out in the solar system.

clue.text: Force coming from member that is left outside

indicators.note: outside means the letters for that is wrap around the letters for member

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Force exerted by a politician who is left outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the abbreviation for that is around the politician; the surface's 'left outside' is a false pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone forward, a synonym of force as a verb.

clue.text: Earl had question with tranquilliser I included for balance

indicators.note: included means the letter I is put inside the string of other pieces

parts.note: Librium is a brand of tranquilliser drug

explanation.surface: An aristocrat questioned while sedated tries to keep his balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts I inside EQU + LIBRIUM, between the question and the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Equilibrium is a state of balance between opposing forces.

clue.text: Drunk on about one and three-quarter pints

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A drinker gets drunk on nearly two pints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is only a link. A litre is about 1.76 imperial pints, so the definition is a fair approximation.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric volume of roughly 1.76 British pints is a litre.

clue.text: It does not keep one fully employed

definitions.text: It does not keep one fully employed

parts.words: It does not keep one fully employed
parts.note: describes work occupying only some of the working week

explanation.definitionFit: Work for fewer hours than a full working week leaves a person less than fully employed.

clue.text: Greek character's hat scheme becoming a lot similar

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: becoming means the letters of hat and scheme turn into something new

explanation.surface: A Greek person's hat plan ends up much like the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' signals the rearrangement of the nine letters of hat and scheme; 'a lot similar' is an unusual but fair gloss of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means largely alike or nearly unchanged, so a lot similar.

clue.text: Not having been in a union for long

definitions.text: Not having been in a union for long

parts.words: Not having been in a union for long
parts.note: suggests someone new to a trade union, but means a couple newly wed

explanation.definitionFit: Newly-weds have been joined in matrimony only a short while.

clue.text: Flame red jacket?

parts.note: a blaze is a flame or fire
R is the abbreviation for red

explanation.surface: A fiery red jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a type of sports or school jacket, an example of one, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Unkempt garment that has been discarded has label on

parts.note: a rag is an old worn-out piece of clothing
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A scruffy cast-off garment still has its label attached.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'has label on' puts the cast-off garment on top of the label.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag means untidy, scruffy or ragged in appearance.

clue.text: Fellow feller

parts.note: a man (fellow) who chops down trees (feller)

explanation.definitionFit: A woodcutter who fells trees with a chopping tool is a man who fells.

clue.text: Reflecting no light this water between Europe and Asia

definitions.text: Reflecting no light this water between Europe and Asia

parts.words: Reflecting no light this water between Europe and Asia
parts.note: a colour that reflects no light names the inland sea bordered by Turkey, Ukraine and others

explanation.definitionFit: The inland sea between south-east Europe and Asia Minor is named for the darkest colour.

clue.text: Potential spoils be distributed

indicators.note: distributed means the letters of spoils and be are spread around into a new order

explanation.surface: The potential spoils of war are to be shared out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something possible has potential to happen, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: One might say this in an appreciative way

definitions.text: One might say this in an appreciative way

parts.words: One might say this in an appreciative way
parts.note: the words a grateful person utters

explanation.definitionFit: Expressing gratitude is done with these two words of appreciation.

clue.text: Hinder unknown number during difficult times

indicators.note: during means the unknown is placed inside the other letters
difficult means the letters of times are made awkward, rearranged

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: An unknown factor hinders progress during hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges TIMES to STMIE; 'during' puts Y inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to obstruct or thwart, a synonym of hinder.

clue.text: Heard cook grating

indicators.note: heard means the word sounds like the one given, when spoken

parts.note: to grill is to cook under direct heat

explanation.surface: Someone heard a cook grating cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grating of bars over a window or opening.

clue.text: Yellow book held in central bank

parts.note: gold is a yellow colour
to book a seat is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A yellow volume is kept inside the central bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold reserve is the bullion a central bank holds to back its currency.

clue.text: Last order before time's up

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for time is read from the bottom

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Final orders are given before time runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the period of time backwards in this down clue; 'time's up' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the last.

clue.text: Duke not well coming up for flag

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word for not well is read upwards

parts.note: poor can mean unwell, as in poor health

explanation.surface: A sickly duke rises to raise a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns the word for unwell backwards in this down clue; 'flag' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or sag, as does droop as a verb.

clue.text: Southern sailors' pay

parts.note: a ship's crew are its sailors

explanation.surface: The wages of sailors from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is old British slang for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is a slang word for salary or wages, so it means pay.

clue.text: Bird coming from city in Brittany, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the city's name is spoken and sounds like the bird

parts.note: Rennes is the capital of Brittany in France

explanation.surface: A bird arriving from a Breton city, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: The wren is a tiny brown songbird.

clue.text: I blame Mario correcting noteworthy points

indicators.note: correcting means the letters of I blame Mario are put right in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone blames Mario while correcting notable details.
explanation.definitionFit: Memorabilia are things worth remembering, notable events or items worth recording.

clue.text: Frenchman repeatedly using the old expression of mild disagreement

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word for the old is used twice

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: A Frenchman keeps using an old-fashioned phrase to disagree mildly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive exclamation meaning nonsense or I doubt it, a mild expression of disbelief.

clue.text: Penny after fighting found buckle

indicators.note: after means the coin letter comes after the word for fighting

parts.note: war is fighting

explanation.surface: A coin found bent after a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To warp is to bend or twist out of shape, a synonym of buckle.

clue.text: Remove agent, not Georgia

indicators.note: not means the letters for Georgia are taken away from the word for agent

parts.note: a delegate is a representative or agent
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: An agent is removed, though not from Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete is to strike out or erase, a synonym of remove.
